items.textToSpeech: For everyone older than 7 months, including those pregnant or lactating, the Population Reference Intake for niacin is 1.6 milligrams of niacin equivalents per megajoule. where 1 milligram of niacin is equivalent to 60 milligrams of dietary tryptophan, an essential amino acid. – 1 megajoule is equivalent to 239 kilocalories. So for example, for a daily intake of 2,000 kilocalories, the Population Reference Intake for niacin is 13.4 milligrams per day. or 804 milligrams of dietary tryptophan.

items.textToSpeech: The Population Reference Intake is the level of nutrient intake that will meet the requirements of 97.5% of the individuals in the population. For the European Union, Dietary Reference Values are published by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies. Is there anything else I can help you with?
